# Application kerning defaults

Six independent, manually authored OOXML packages are generated by
`tools/default_kerning_fixture.py`. They contain eight original text rows each,
using installed Arial and Times New Roman with omitted, zero, 1pt and 100pt
kerning thresholds. No corpus content or font binaries are included.

`tools/export-default-kerning.ps1` opens each exact source read-only in the
reference application, captures paragraph kerning thresholds and exports a one-page PDF.
`tools/record_default_kerning.py` independently extracts native character
origins and binds the source, authored cases, COM observations and PDFs by hash.
Regenerating sources requires new native exports and recording.

An absent `rPrDefault` invokes a 1pt application threshold, including an absent
styles part or an empty `docDefaults`. A present empty `rPrDefault`, with or
without an empty `rPr`, leaves the threshold zero. An explicit default of 6pt
is inherited. Direct zero, 1pt and 100pt declarations override all six cases.
The 14pt text visibly distinguishes enabled and disabled pairs.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.7.5.5 permits application-defined defaults when the category
is absent; §17.3.2.19 defines explicit kerning thresholds. This is reference consumer
behavior, not a contradiction of those clauses. It does not change defaults
for new editor documents, which already serialize `rPrDefault`.

Tests retain native thresholds, line strings, baselines and the final period's
origin, plus native editing, exact no-edit/undo packages, unrelated parts and
reopening. Internal caret boundaries are not treated as glyph origins for
kerned pairs. These controls do not resolve version differences or absent
kerning tables in the separately reviewed Open Sans assets.
